representative_tasks.task: Explain how an LSTM's gates and additive cell-state update mitigate vanishing gradients
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Describes forget/input/output gates and the additive cell path; says gating reduces but does not eliminate the problem

representative_tasks.task: LSTM vs GRU for a new sequence task
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Notes GRU has about 3/4 of the parameters and no consistent winner in comparisons; recommends trying both when it matters

representative_tasks.task: Fix truncated-BPTT errors when carrying hidden state across chunks
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Detaches the carried state at chunk boundaries and removes retain_graph=True

representative_tasks.task: Pick the sentence representation from a padded, stacked, bidirectional GRU
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Packs the sequences and concatenates h_n[-2] and h_n[-1]; explains why output[:, -1] is wrong and that a lengths - 1 / position-0 gather is valid only on the packed run's output (unpacked, no position of a 2-layer bidirectional output is clean)

negative_cases: Misconception that LSTMs have no vanishing-gradient problem and that the 1997 LSTM had a forget gate (planned)
Ambiguous request whether to use an RNN instead of a transformer in 2026, where the answer must condition on streaming/on-device constraints (planned)
rubric: Gives the root cause (graph still attached through carried state; padding read by the RNN) before the fix
Uses correct PyTorch semantics: .detach() at chunk boundaries, pack_padded_sequence with enforce_sorted=False, h_n layout independent of batch_first
Distinguishes forward and backward directions when extracting a bidirectional summary
Backs out a wrong earlier fix instead of layering workarounds on it
execution_constraints: Offline grading and fixture self-tests need only Python 3.10+ stdlib and no network.
Model-mode runs need --provider anthropic --model <id> --allow-network and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; they cost money and are not deterministic.
known_limitations: Hard assertions are regexes over the response text: they verify that key concepts are stated, not that the reasoning connecting them is correct.
No baseline (with-skill vs without-skill) has been measured for this skill; any uplift claim requires a recorded or model run.
Both cases are PyTorch-specific; the h_n layout and error messages differ in other frameworks.

Paraphrase robustness was spot-checked once with 4 answers written by the pattern author after the patterns were set (one correct and one wrong per case): before any fix, 1/2 correct answers passed and 2/2 wrong answers failed. Misses were fixed by broadening patterns and all 4 answers were kept as .probe fixtures, so they are no longer held out and the probe was not blind.

Independent probe (Phase 2 review): 7 answers for this skill's cases written by a reviewer who did not write the patterns, graded once before any change. Before the fix 2/3 correct answers passed and only 0/4 plausible on-topic wrong answers failed (31 answers across the five skills of this workstream: 11/14 correct passed, 5/16 wrong failed). Most misses were hedge-word escape hatches ('only', 'not', 'if') that fired on the wrong answer's own wording, and concept patterns satisfied by negated mentions. The patterns were then fixed and the reviewer's answers kept verbatim as .pass.blind* / .fail.adversarial* fixtures, so they now grade as expected only because the patterns were tuned to them and are no longer held out.

Fix-engineer probe: 4 further answers (.pass.fixprobe / .fail.fixprobe) written by the engineer who then edited the patterns, after reading the review but before editing, graded once: 1/2 correct passed and 2/2 wrong failed before the fix (8/10 and 8/10 across the five skills). This is author-adjacent, not blind, and the answers are now fixtures. Expect real model outputs to find further phrasings that neither probe anticipated; the rubric remains authoritative.
unsupported_use_cases: Classical time-series forecasting such as ARIMA/Prophet (time-series)
